question: Extend the governance extract to the full DAFRC FY2024 frame (1,429 sponsors ranked 51+ with DAF assets > 0, plus the top 50) instead of a 100-sponsor sample, to put intervals on band prevalences and to list every sponsor answering 'No' to Part VI lines 12a, 13 and 14
conclusion_affected: Band prevalence of policies and audits below $10m of DAF assets (n = 57 in this sample)
rationale: In the 100-sponsor sample, every 'No' to the conflict-of-interest (8), whistleblower (17) and document-retention (13) questions falls in the < $10m band; with 57 sponsors in that band the share is imprecise. The script is already parameterised (SEED, SAMPLE_N); all returns came from the GivingTuesday mirror or local caches

question: Do sponsors' own financial statements explain why their Form 990 reports no separate audit (Part XII line 2b = No)? For American Gift Fund (TY2022-2023) and National Christian Charitable Foundation (TY2022), check whether they were covered by consolidated audited statements, which the instructions say must be answered 'No' unless a separate audit was received
conclusion_affected: Whether the 'not audited' years at two top-50 sponsors reflect a consolidated audit or no audit
rationale: IRS instructions for Part XII line 2b say to answer 'No' if the organisation was included only in consolidated audited statements. Both sponsors answered 'Yes' in later years. The Form 990 alone cannot tell the two cases apart

question: Excess-benefit transactions involving donor advisors: collect every 2021+ Schedule L Part I filed by any DAFRC sponsor (not only this 150-sponsor population), coding the relationship (donor advisor, family member, investment adviser), the amount, the 4958 tax and the correction, to size how often section 4958(c)(2) DAF rules are reported
conclusion_affected: How common reported DAF excess-benefit transactions are; whether they cluster at sponsors with advisor-managed DAF programmes
rationale: In this population only NPT (TY2022-2024; de minimis adviser compensation paid by a third-party investment manager, reported as corrected) and Servant Foundation (TY2022; two donor-advisor transactions 'subject to the tax pursuant to IRC section 4958(c)(2)') answer Yes to Part IV 25a

question: Part VI line 15a and line 3 at affiliate-staffed sponsors: for the top-50 sponsors with zero employees on Part I line 5 (15), read the services agreements or Schedule O text that say who sets pay for the people who run the sponsor; check whether any sponsor discloses the affiliate's compensation process
conclusion_affected: Interpretation of 'No' to 15a at commercial-affiliate sponsors (instructions count only a process the filing organisation used, not one used by a related organisation)
rationale: All 11 top-50 sponsors answering 'No' to 15a in TY2024 report zero employees on Part I line 5. Fidelity Charitable leaves 15a/15b blank in all three years. The compensation direction flags these sponsors as affiliate-staffed or as having a top officer paid by a related organisation

question: Re-run the governance extract when TY2025 returns are indexed (IRS index_2026 / index_2027) and record answer changes year on year, to test whether the TY2022-2024 stability (no conflict-of-interest answer changed; 13 audit-status changes, mostly No->Yes) persists
rationale: Answers are very stable over TY2022-2024: no sponsor changed its 12a or line 6 answer; 2 changed 13, 4 changed 14 and 13 changed their audit status. One more year would show whether audit take-up continues among small community foundations
